<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

The Quark Kimi-K3 checkpoint (`Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) stores the shared experts in MXFP4 and leaves the router and the latent down-projection in BF16. `KimiK3MoE._merge_front_weights` concatenates only dense weights, so on ROCm these MoE layers get no merged front and run `_forward_unfused`. There the shared gate-up and down run as separate W4A4 GEMMs, with online MXFP4 activation quantization, next to separate router and latent GEMMs.

This PR adds an opt-in switch that dequantizes those shared experts to BF16 once, at load. The existing merged front and the fused single-collective path (`_forward_fused`) then cover these layers too. Decode is up to 5% faster, and GSM8K improves from 93.6% to 96.8%: with the W4A4 shared experts, 3.7% of answers turned into runaway generations, and with the switch on there are none.

## Modifications

- `QuarkW4A4MXFP4.dequantize_to_bf16` is the existing `AITER_FORCE_A8W4` dequantize step, moved into a method and made idempotent. `create_weights` always sets `layer.dequantized_bf16`, `process_weights_after_loading` skips a linear that is already densified, and `apply_weights` reads the field directly instead of through `getattr`.
- `kimi_k3_rocm_quant.densify_quark_mxfp4_shared_experts` is called from `KimiK3MoE._merge_front_weights`, behind `_is_hip` and the switch, only where the full front can be built (shared experts present, no MoE all-to-all backend).
- The switch is `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_QUARK_SHARED_FULL_FRONT`, off by default, documented in `environ.py` and the AMD & ROCm table of the environment variable reference. With it off, nothing changes. CUDA and other checkpoints are not affected.
- `test_kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py` tests that densifying and the loader's post-processing commute. Two orders are covered:
  - Model first, as with `DefaultModelLoader`.
  - Loader first, as with the sharded-state and remote-instance loaders under `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1`.

  In both, each weight must be decoded exactly once. Removing either guard makes the test fail.
- Memory: at TP8, BF16 shared experts take 24 MB more per MoE layer than MXFP4, or 2.2 GB per GPU over K3's 92 MoE layers. Measured on the server below, the KV cache and KDA state budget fell by 2.75 GB per GPU (40.4 to 37.7 GB), because some of the freed MXFP4 blocks stay in the allocator. The docs give the measured figure.
- The cookbook is unchanged. Its MI35x recipe serves `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, whose shared experts are already BF16, and the switch stays off by default.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3 on all 1319 questions, using the `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` preset (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on, reasoning_effort max, max_tokens 300000) and 64 threads. Each switch setting has its own server, with the configuration below and the radix cache on (the cookbook default). One run each.

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --model /data/models/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-threads 64
```

| | Switch off | Switch on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Score | 93.56% | 96.82% |
| Answers longer than 4096 tokens | 49 (longest 104,830; 3 correct) | 0 (longest 4,056) |
| Score on answers of at most 4096 tokens | 96.93% | 96.82% |
| Mean output tokens | 1,265 | 123 |
| Truncated / errors | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The whole gap comes from the runaway answers. On the rest, the two settings score the same.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, `/data/models/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`. SGLang is `main` @ `2815eed49c` plus this change. The PR head carries the same code on a newer `main`; only the docs wording differs. AITER is the image's `2bb549102`.

The server is the cookbook MI355X Unified Balanced recipe, Non-Spec:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE=1 \
SGLANG_AITER_HONOR_EXPLICIT_MEM_FRACTION=1 SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_QUARK_SHARED_FULL_FRONT={0,1} \
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/models/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --dtype bfloat16 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \
  --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --disable-radix-cache
```

Differences from the cookbook:
- The Quark checkpoint instead of `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`.
- Non-Spec instead of DSPARK.
- `SGLANG_AITER_HONOR_EXPLICIT_MEM_FRACTION=1`. Without it, the AITER long-context scaling turns 0.85 into 0.7225, which leaves about 6 GB for KV cache and state and limits admission to 11 requests.
- `--disable-radix-cache`, for the speed sweep only. The seed-42 random prompts repeat across levels, so with the radix cache on, later levels hit prefixes that earlier levels cached, and the two servers evict differently.

Client, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens, 4 waves per concurrency (at least 8 prompts), 32 warmup requests before the first level:

```bash
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency C --num-prompts 4C --request-rate inf --seed 42
```

| Conc | TPOT (ms) off | TPOT (ms) on | Δ | TTFT (ms) off | TTFT (ms) on | Δ | Output tok/s/GPU off | Output tok/s/GPU on | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 19.17 | 18.19 | -5.1% | 490 | 483 | -1.4% | 6.4 | 6.7 | +5.3% |
| 4 | 22.18 | 21.23 | -4.3% | 1574 | 1555 | -1.2% | 21.1 | 22.0 | +4.2% |
| 8 | 25.63 | 24.42 | -4.8% | 2622 | 2613 | -0.3% | 35.5 | 37.1 | +4.5% |
| 16 | 29.94 | 28.96 | -3.3% | 4648 | 4661 | +0.3% | 58.0 | 59.7 | +2.9% |
| 32 | 38.32 | 37.61 | -1.8% | 8220 | 8254 | +0.4% | 86.4 | 87.6 | +1.5% |
| 64 | 54.50 | 53.91 | -1.1% | 15293 | 15385 | +0.6% | 115.3 | 116.1 | +0.7% |

A first sweep with the radix cache on gave the same TPOT gains at concurrency 1 to 32 (-5.2% to -1.8%).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks passed.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py`: 7 passed. With either guard removed, the new case fails.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `a57c04b`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44049/checks?check_run_id=119748444257)

Closing: not needed for Kimi-K3. The Quark checkpoint (`Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) lists every `shared_experts.{gate,up,down}_proj` in its quantization `exclude` list, so the shared experts already load in BF16 and join the merged MoE front without a load-time densify. The densify has nothing to convert, and our K3 integration branch has dropped it.

files.patch: @@ -1907,6 +1907,11 @@ SGLang supports various environment variables that can be used to configure its Token count above which SGLANG_ROCM_K3_FUSE_KDA_INPROJ stops applying and the split projection runs instead. The merged shape is only faster while the projection is bandwidth bound. 256 + + SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_QUARK_SHARED_FULL_FRONT + Kimi-K3 on ROCm with a Quark MXFP4 checkpoint: dequantize the shared experts to BF16 at load so the MoE runs the merged front (shared gate-up, router and latent down-projection in one GEMM) instead of the unfused path. Applies without an MoE all-to-all backend. At TP8 it leaves about 2.8 GB less per GPU for the KV cache and KDA state. + false +

@@ -2002,6 +2002,9 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_K3_FUSED_FRONT = EnvBool(True)
     # Use the ROCm radix-4 router for covered K3 top-k workloads.
     SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK = EnvBool(False)
+    # Dequantize Quark MXFP4 shared experts to BF16 at load so they join the
+    # merged Kimi-K3 MoE front on ROCm; at TP8 this takes ~2.8 GB/GPU from the KV pool.
+    SGLANG_OPT_HIP_K3_QUARK_SHARED_FULL_FRONT = EnvBool(False)
     SGLANG_KIMI_K3_VIT_CUDA_GRAPH_CACHE_CAPACITY = EnvInt(2)
     SGLANG_KIMI_K3_VIT_CUDA_GRAPH_MIN_HITS = EnvInt(2)
     SGLANG_KIMI_K3_VIT_CUDA_GRAPH_MAX_SEQLEN = EnvInt(6144)

@@ -406,17 +406,30 @@ def __init__(
     def get_min_capability(cls) -> int:
         return 70
 
+    def dequantize_to_bf16(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        """Switch the linear to a dense BF16 weight and GEMM. Idempotent: the
+        model and the loader may each request it, in either order."""
+        if layer.dequantized_bf16:
+            return
+        # The ASM layout (shuffled weight, swizzled scale) no longer decodes as MXFP4.
+        if layer.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm:
+            return
+        w_bf16 = _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(layer.weight.data, layer.weight_scale.data)
+        layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w_bf16, requires_grad=False)
+        # FP4 block scales are folded into the bf16 weight; drop them.
+        layer.weight_scale = None
+        layer.dequantized_bf16 = True
+
     def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        # A model may already have densified this linear before the loader pass.
+        if layer.dequantized_bf16:
+            return
         if not self.is_checkpoint_mxfp4_serialized:
             assert layer.weight.dtype == torch.uint8
             assert layer.weight_scale.dtype == torch.uint8
 
         if _dequant_linear_to_bf16:
-            w_bf16 = _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(layer.weight.data, layer.weight_scale.data)
-            layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w_bf16, requires_grad=False)
-            # FP4 block scales are folded into the bf16 weight; drop them.
-            layer.weight_scale = None
-            layer.dequantized_bf16 = True
+            self.dequantize_to_bf16(layer)
             return
 
         layer.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm = False
@@ -463,6 +476,8 @@ def create_weights(
         **kwargs,
     ):
         self.input_size_per_partition = input_size_per_partition
+        layer.dequantized_bf16 = False
+        layer.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm = False
 
         output_size_per_partition = sum(output_partition_sizes)
         self.output_size_per_partition = output_size_per_partition
@@ -861,17 +876,17 @@ def apply_weights(
         x: torch.Tensor,
         bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
-        # bf16 fallback: FP4 weights were dequantized to bf16 at load time
-        # because this HW cannot run the fp4 GEMM. Run a plain bf16 linear.
+        # FP4 weights were dequantized to bf16 at load, because this HW cannot
+        # run the fp4 GEMM or the model densified the linear. Run a plain bf16 linear.
         # (The fused tuple-input paths below are only used by MLA attention
         # projections, which are excluded from quantization for this checkpoint,
         # so a plain-tensor activation is what reaches here.)
-        if getattr(layer, "dequantized_bf16", False):
+        if layer.dequantized_bf16:
             if isinstance(x, tuple):
                 x = x[0]
             return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, layer.weight, bias)
 
-        if getattr(layer, "use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm", False):
+        if layer.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm:
             output_shape = None
             if isinstance(x, tuple):
                 x_q, x_scales = _asm_fp4_prequantized_input(x)

@@ -729,6 +729,12 @@ def _merge_front_weights(self) -> None:
         if not (get_platform().is_cuda or get_platform().is_hip):

### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `a57c04b`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44049/checks?check_run_id=119748444257)

Closing: not needed for Kimi-K3. The Quark checkpoint (`Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`) lists every `shared_experts.{gate,up,down}_proj` in its quantization `exclude` list, so the shared experts already load in BF16 and join the merged MoE front without a load-time densify. The densify has nothing to convert, and our K3 integration branch has dropped it.
